content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: overtime for 13 payments agents, callbacks on both queues, a 45-minute delay to general breaks and chat deflection. It is predicted to reach 81.2% service level for 12:15-14:15 at an extra cost of ₹2,004.","why":"Payments handle time has climbed from about 291-299 s forecast to 560 s by 12:00. Call volume and staffing are on plan, so the problem is longer calls, not more of them. The likely cause is the CardMax slowness ticket INC-20261019-1835. That link is not yet confirmed: the ticket is a P4 opened at 12:05. Service level recovered to 96.7% at 12:00 only because 50 agents were on the phones against 39 planned. With no action, service level is predicted to fall to 68.0% (payments 63.4%) during 12:15-14:15. R2 is the only option that reaches the 80% target over that window: 81.2% overall, payments 78.5%, general 84.7%, abandon rate 5.5%. It breaks no policy rules. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 89.7%.","trade_offs":["Cost: R2 costs ₹2,004. That is ₹204 more than R1 (₹1,800), which only reaches 74.8%. It is ₹156 less than P2 and P3 (₹2,160 each), which reach only 77.4% and 74.5%.","Payments stays below target: even under R2, payments is predicted at 78.5% while general carries the overall figure at 84.7%.","Effect on general: R2 delays general breaks 13:15-13:45 by 45 minutes. General still does well in this window (84.7%, against 73.8% with no action).","Rest of day: P2 has a slightly better rest-of-day figure (90.0% against 89.7%) and is close on abandon rate, but it misses the target during the disruption window.","The no-cost option, P1, barely helps: 69.0% overall and 62.3% on payments."],"watch":"Watch payments handle time and the CardMax ticket. If handle time keeps rising beyond 560 s, or the ticket is confirmed and not fixed by 14:15, these predictions will be optimistic and the plan should be reviewed. Escalation is not flagged. Check overtime uptake from the 13 agents by 12:45, because the plan depends on it."}
